author: Latin Business Daily
title: Ecuador signs USD 30 million investment contract for Block 94 - Tamya oil exploration
text:
Ecuador signs USD 30 million investment contract for Block 94 – Tamya oil exploration
The Ministry of Environment and Energy announced on Aug. 12 the signing of a Participation Contract for the exploration and development of Block 94 – Tamya, located in Sucumbíos, with operator Petrobell S.A. The agreement includes a committed investment of USD 30 million dedicated to exploration activities.
This contract marks the successful conclusion of the Intracampos II bidding round, an initiative by the National Government aimed at attracting private investment, promoting new hydrocarbon resource exploration and development, and strengthening national production. With Block 94 – Tamya, all planned contracts within this round have been finalized.
The contract is valid for 24 years until 2050, divided into two phases: four years for exploration and twenty years for exploitation and comprehensive block development. Authorities say this milestone supports long-term objectives for hydrocarbon resource utilization, job creation, and local investment.
Block Tamya is projected as an oil field with considerable potential. Production could reach an estimated peak of approximately 4,000 barrels of crude per day, which would contribute to government plans to add new reserves and gradually increase total national oil output.
Minister Juan Carlos Blum said about these agreements, “The contract that we signed is a Participation type contract, which means private companies assume the risk and financing of exploration and exploitation activities; the State does not invest any resources. This is a milestone that will strengthen development in Sucumbíos province.”
Officials say implementing this contract supports government policy focused on attracting private investment to boost the hydrocarbon sector, stimulate exploratory activity in promising areas, and generate economic benefits through future increases in production.
